note: The Eras level. Sourced areas carry the cited periods of a published periodization (cite); elsewhere, and after an area's last period, the region's period bins per lane group (basis: period-bin), kept only where the data records a state or culture. Leaders are computed from the spans: most lane-years, weighted by tier.

areas.label: Scandinavia
areas.note: The periods of the list of archaeological periods’ Northern Europe row. The list does not say which countries the row covers; the area is the three Scandinavian countries, an editorial choice (the row’s Nordic Bronze Age and Viking Age are named for Scandinavia). The row gives no dates for the Stone Age or for the Industrial/Modern period, so the period bins are used before the Nordic Bronze Age and after c. 1800.

areas.label: Ireland
areas.note: The dated section headings of History of Ireland, from prehistory to the present. The article treats Northern Ireland in a section of its own, which this column does not use.

areas.label: Greece
areas.note: The dated section headings of History of Greece. The article leaves the stretch between the Fourth Crusade (1204) and the 15th century without a dated heading (its sections there are headed 1204 and “to 1453”), so that stretch stays blank. A century heading is read as the whole century, which is why its start is marked approximate.

areas.label: Netherlands
areas.note: The dated section headings of History of the Netherlands up to 1839. The article’s Prehistory heading is dated only “before 57 BC”, so the period bins are used there, and again from 1840.

areas.label: France
areas.note: The dated section headings of History of France up to 1815. The article’s later headings are bare year ranges (1815–1914, 1914–1945) or “Since 1945”, so the period bins are used from 1816.

areas.label: Iceland
areas.note: The dated section headings of History of Iceland, from the settlement to the present.

areas.label: Switzerland
areas.note: The dated section headings of History of Switzerland, which begin with the Old Confederacy; the period bins are used before 1300.

areas.label: Russia
areas.note: The dated section headings of History of Russia. The article’s own dates overlap (Kievan Rus’ to 1240, the Mongol invasion and vassalage from 1223, the Grand Duchy of Moscow from 1283), and the chart shows the overlaps as written. The column covers Russia west of 60°E.

areas.label: Bulgaria
areas.note: The dated section headings of History of Bulgaria from the First Bulgarian Empire to 1991; the period bins are used before 681 and from 1992.

areas.label: Croatia
areas.note: The dated section headings of History of Croatia, from the Duchy of Croatia to the present; the period bins are used before 800.

areas.label: Bosnia and Herzegovina
areas.note: The dated section headings of History of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which begin with the Ottoman era; the period bins are used before 1463.

areas.label: Moldova
areas.note: The dated section headings of History of Moldova. The article’s Principality of Moldavia (to 1862) and Bessarabia under the Russian Empire (from 1812) overlap, and the chart shows that as written; the period bins are used before 1346.
